"Are you sure these changes are within spec?" A rather weary technician looks over the work of a new hire, who was fiddling with some settings in a control box that oversaw dozens of satellite dishes.

"Oh yea, it's totally safe. I've done it many of times before." The new hire gives a thumbs up. The tone in his voice is convincing and yet unsettling. He turns one last screw before slamming the cover back onto the machine. "And it's done."

"So what will this do again?" The older tech bristles his graying mustache.

"Only answer the great question mankind has ever known: Does ramen taste better when you cook it by the energy of the stars themselves.

The tech pondered this for only a second before giving a dumbfounded "What?" A look of terror grows across his face in a growing intensity like a derailing train dumping more and more coal into a forest fire.

"Now do you think Alpha Centauri or Cygnus X-1 will give it the right consistency?" The new hire contemplates as he flicks some switches to change the orientation of the dishes. "Probably Cygnus X-1."

The tech had no reply. The only thought running through his head was to make a quick egress so anything that happened didn't become his fault. With a blank expression on his face, he left the room and carried on other duties while trying to maintain distance from the new hire. It wasn't until break that he saw the new hire in the break room, eating some piping hot ramen.

"I thought we didn't have a microwave here." the tech inquires.

"We don't. They interfere with the equipment."

"Oh."

I think you're coming along well, you have some neat ideas. Here are some constructive criticisms, please don't take them the wrong way, advice is worth what you pay for it! 1. You're playing has a rough sound, which can be an asset depending on what you're going for, but I think it's a little too loose. Improving your timing is one of the biggest things you can do to improve your playing. 2. When you strum, you need to learn when to do an upstroke vs a downstroke. This is really hard to describe, and it's one of the first difficulties I see with beginners. I try to describe it in terms of efficiency. If you have enough time to return to the low E, go ahead and play another downstroke instead of an upstroke. Only play downstrokes when the pattern is too fast/ dense for you to play downstrokes. 3. Your guitar may be slightly out of tune, you may be pressing on light strings with too much force, or you may be resting your hand on the floating bridge, causing the pitch to shift. Whatever the cause, there are times where your guitar sounds really out of tune.

If you make these adjustments, you'll be well on your way! I hope my criticisms weren't too harsh.
